incoming.excerpt: Seacoast Angelica (A. lucida) has been eaten as a sort of "wild celery".

outgoing.name: English language
outgoing.excerpt: It passed through Latin, Italian and French before becoming the modern English word celery.

outgoing.name: Flower
outgoing.excerpt: The flowers are creamy-white, 2-3 mm diameter, produced in dense compound umbels.

outgoing.name: Latin
outgoing.excerpt: There is a widespread popular etymology that the word celery ("The Fast Vegetable") derives from the Latin word, celer, meaning fast or swift.
